# Configuration

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:config` from server/src/config.ts and server/src/configMeta.ts. Do not edit by hand: `docs:check` fails when it is stale. -->

Every setting is an environment variable, validated at start-up by a zod schema (`server/src/config.ts`); an invalid value stops the process with a message naming the variable. Defaults make `npm run dev` work with no environment at all. Booleans accept `true|false|1|0`. There are **116** variables; the ones marked **Secret** must come from your secret store, never from the repository.

Start-up cross-checks: `SMS_PROVIDER=twilio` needs the Twilio credentials, `EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid` needs `SENDGRID_API_KEY`, `SOCKET_ADAPTER=redis` or `JOB_QUEUE=bullmq` need `REDIS_URL`, `DATABASE_URL` must be a `postgres://` URL, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` needs `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and production needs `JWT_SECRET`.

## Core

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | `development` \| `test` \| `production` | `development` | no | `production` | Runtime mode. `production` requires `JWT_SECRET`; `test` is used by the test suite. |
| `PORT` | integer (min 0, max 65535) | `3000` | no | `3000` | TCP port the HTTP and Socket.IO server listens on (0 = random free port). |
| `HOST` | string | `0.0.0.0` | no | `0.0.0.0` | Interface to bind. |
| `WEB_DIST` | string | unset | no |  | Directory of the built web app to serve (default `../web/dist`). |
| `JWT_SECRET` | string | unset | production | `openssl rand -hex 32` | Signing secret for access tokens (and the key from which MFA secrets are encrypted and platform-admin tokens are derived; the analytics identity pepper no longer depends on it, see `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`). At least 16 characters. Required in production; in development an ephemeral secret is generated and tokens die on restart. **Secret.** Rotating it signs everyone out, invalidates MFA enrolments stored encrypted with it and ends platform-admin tokens. Use the same value on every node. |
| `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | string | unset | no | `openssl rand -hex 32` | Key that encrypts long-lived secrets at rest, today the analytics identity pepper: 32 random bytes as 64 hex characters or base64. Required in production once analytics is used (the pepper endpoint and the exports answer `503 DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_REQUIRED` without it); in development a key is derived from `JWT_SECRET` with a warning. Existing peppers encrypted under `JWT_SECRET` are re-encrypted under this key the first time they are read. **Secret.** Unlike `JWT_SECRET` it must not be rotated casually: losing it makes stored peppers unreadable (`409 PEPPER_UNREADABLE`; set a new pepper to recover). To rotate it, move the old value to `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`. Use the same value on every node. |
| `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS` | string | unset | no | `(the old DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` | Previous `DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` value or values (comma separated), still accepted for decryption while a rotation re-encrypts stored secrets under the new key on their next read. Remove it once every workspace that uses analytics has been read once. **Secret.** |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` | integer (> 0) | `900` | no | `900` | Lifetime of an access token. Clients renew it with the refresh token (30 days, single use, rotated). |
| `PUBLIC_URL` | string | `http://localhost:3000` | no | `https://chat.example.com` | Public base URL of this installation. Used in emailed links (invitations, password reset, notifications), signed file URLs, Stripe return URLs and the widget. |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | string | `http://localhost:5173` | no | `https://app.example.com` | Comma-separated origins allowed to call the team API from a browser. The widget endpoints (`/public/*`) accept any origin and are protected by the embed token's domain binding instead. |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | boolean | `false` | no |  | Believe `X-Forwarded-For` / `CF-Connecting-IP` for the client address. Turn on only behind a proxy you control. With it off, every client appears to come from the proxy and per-IP limits would hit everyone at once; with it on and no proxy, clients can spoof their address. |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` | integer (min 1, max 10) | `1` | no | `2` | Number of proxies of ours that append to `X-Forwarded-For`; the client address is the entry this many from the right (so a client-supplied prefix is ignored). |
| `BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` | integer (> 0) | `1048576` | no |  | Maximum JSON request body. |
| `REGION` | string | unset | no | `eu-west` | Region this installation serves (for example `eu-west`). A workspace whose home region (set by an operator) differs is refused with `421 WRONG_REGION` and the right region in `details.region`, so a global edge or load balancer can route it home. Unset = single region, no check. |
| `CF_SHARED_SECRET` | string | unset | no |  | Secret that the Cloudflare Worker adds as `x-edge-secret`; only requests carrying it have `CF-Connecting-IP` believed. See docs/CLOUDFLARE.md. **Secret.** |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer (> 0) | `30000` | no |  | Per-request timeout for `/api` and `/public` (504 after it). |

## Database

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_PATH` | string | `./data/conversations.db` | no | `./data/conversations.db` | SQLite file used when `DATABASE_URL` is unset (`:memory:` for tests). |
| `DATABASE_URL` | string | unset | no | `postgres://app:***@db:5432/conversations` | `postgres://` URL. Setting it switches to PostgreSQL (multi-node). Contains credentials. **Secret.** |
| `MESSAGE_HASH_PARTITIONS` | integer (min 1, max 256) | `16` | no | `16` | Hash partitions of the `messages` table (by room). Read once, when the partitioning migration first runs on PostgreSQL; cannot be changed afterwards without a rebuild. |
| `MESSAGE_PARTITION_MONTHS_AHEAD` | integer (min 0, max 24) | `3` | no |  | Monthly partitions created ahead of time by the daily job. |
| `DATABASE_PGBOUNCER` | boolean | `false` | no |  | Set when a transaction-mode PgBouncer sits between the app and PostgreSQL: disables named prepared statements. The app uses no other session state. |
| `DATABASE_REPLICA_URL` | string | unset | no |  | Optional read replica for history, list, search and analytics reads (`Db.read()`), with a lag guard and read-your-writes fallback to the primary. **Secret.** |
| `DATABASE_REPLICA_MAX_LAG_MS` | integer (min 0) | `1000` | no |  | Reads fall back to the primary when the replica lags more than this. |
| `DATABASE_READ_AFTER_WRITE_MS` | integer (min 0) | `1500` | no |  | After a write, reads for the same workspace/room go to the primary for this long. |
| `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` | integer (> 0) | `10` | no |  | PostgreSQL pool size per node. Sizing formula in docs/SCALING.md. |

| `DATA_DIR` | string | `./data` | no | `/data` | Directory for uploads and local data. |

## Redis and scale-out

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SOCKET_ADAPTER` | `auto` \| `memory` \| `redis` | `auto` | no |  | Socket.IO adapter: `auto` = Redis when `REDIS_URL` is set, else in-memory. |
| `REDIS_URL` | string | unset | no | `redis://redis:6379` | Redis URL. Setting it enables the shared rate limiter, presence, cache invalidation, locks, the Socket.IO adapter, the event bus and the job queue. **Secret.** |
| `REDIS_PREFIX` | string | `conv` | no |  | Namespace for every Redis key and channel, so several environments can share one Redis. |
| `JOB_QUEUE` | `auto` \| `db` \| `bullmq` | `auto` | no |  | `db` = jobs table polled by the scheduler, `bullmq` = BullMQ on Redis, `auto` = BullMQ when Redis is configured. |
| `CACHE_TTL_MS` | integer (min 0) | `3000` | no |  | Lifetime of the small in-process caches (seat, settings, counts). Changes are invalidated across nodes through Redis; this is the staleness bound when Redis is down. |
| `PRESENCE_TTL_MS` | integer (> 0) | `30000` | no |  | Presence entries expire after this long without a heartbeat (shared presence on Redis). |
| `PRESENCE_GRACE_MS` | integer (min 0) | `5000` | no |  | A socket that disconnects is shown offline only after this grace period (page reloads do not flap). |

## Operations

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ID` | string | unset | no |  | Identifier of this process in logs, metrics and Redis keys. Default: hostname plus random suffix. |
| `METRICS_TOKEN` | string | unset | no |  | Bearer token required for `GET /metrics`. Unset = open (private network only). **Secret.** |
| `SENTRY_DSN` | string | unset | no |  | Sentry DSN for server error monitoring. Unset = monitoring is off: the SDK is not loaded and nothing is sent. See docs/MONITORING.md for what is and is not sent. **Secret.** A DSN only allows sending events, but treat it as configuration, not as public text. |
| `SENTRY_WEB_DSN` | string | unset | no |  | DSN handed to the web app at runtime (`/runtime-config.json`) for browser error monitoring. Defaults to SENTRY_DSN; set a separate Sentry project here to keep browser noise apart. A browser DSN is visible to every visitor of the app by design. |
| `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` | string | unset | no |  | Environment tag on Sentry events (`production`, `staging`). Defaults to NODE_ENV. |
| `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE` | number (min 0, max 1) | `0.05` | no |  | Fraction (0 to 1) of requests sampled for Sentry performance traces. Errors are always captured; set 0 to disable tracing. |
| `SENTRY_RELEASE` | string | unset | no |  | Release name on Sentry events. Defaults to RENDER_GIT_COMMIT (set by Render), then GIT_SHA. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `debug` \| `info` \| `warn` \| `error` \| `silent` | `info` | no |  | Minimum log level. Logs are JSON lines; message content and secrets are never logged. |

## WebSocket and realtime

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WS_PING_INTERVAL_MS` | integer (> 0) | `25000` | no |  | Socket.IO ping interval. |
| `WS_PING_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer (> 0) | `20000` | no |  | Socket.IO ping timeout. |
| `WS_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES` | integer (> 0) | `262144` | no |  | Largest single socket message. |
| `WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | integer (min 0) | `0` | no |  | Concurrent sockets per node (0 = unlimited). New connections beyond it are shed with 503 and a jittered retry hint. |
| `WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP` | integer (min 0) | `0` | no |  | Concurrent sockets per client IP, cluster-wide (0 = unlimited). |
| `WS_CONNECT_RATE_PER_IP` | number (> 0) | `20` | no |  | Socket handshakes per second per IP (reconnect storms). |
| `WS_MAX_WRITE_BUFFER` | integer (> 0) | `500` | no |  | A socket whose outbound queue exceeds this many packets is a slow consumer and is disconnected. |
| `WS_DRAIN_MS` | integer (min 0) | `5000` | no |  | On shutdown, how long clients get to reconnect elsewhere (staggered) before the node closes. |
| `WS_PERMESSAGE_DEFLATE` | boolean | `false` | no |  | Compress socket frames. Off by default: measured to cost more CPU and memory than it saves (docs/adr/0009-permessage-deflate-off.md). |
| `WS_TRANSPORTS` | `websocket` \| `polling,websocket` \| `websocket,polling` | `polling,websocket` | no |  | Allowed Socket.IO transports. |
| `WS_MAX_HANDSHAKES` | integer (> 0) | `500` | no |  | Concurrent in-flight handshakes per node before new ones are shed. |
| `WS_STRIKE_LIMIT` | integer (> 0) | `25` | no |  | Rate-limited socket events tolerated before the socket is disconnected. |
| `WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_WORKSPACE` | integer (min 0) | `0` | no |  | Concurrent sockets per workspace, cluster-wide (0 = unlimited; with `PLAN_ENFORCEMENT` the plan tier applies). |
| `SOCKET_RATE_PER_SEC` | number (> 0) | `10` | no |  | Per-socket event budget refill (events/second); events have costs (typing is cheap, sending is dear). |
| `SOCKET_RATE_BURST` | number (> 0) | `30` | no |  | Per-socket event burst. |

## Rate limiting and overload

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PLAN_ENFORCEMENT` | boolean | `false` | no |  | Enforce plan limits that need billing to be meaningful: socket caps per plan, seat limits, and the soft lock after a failed payment. Plan-scaled request limits are always on. |
| `RATELIMIT_REDIS_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer (> 0) | `30` | no |  | Budget for one limiter call to Redis; on timeout the policy's fail-open/closed rule applies. |
| `RATELIMIT_BREAKER_FAILURES` | integer (> 0) | `5` | no |  | Consecutive Redis failures that open the limiter's circuit breaker. |
| `RATELIMIT_BREAKER_OPEN_MS` | integer (> 0) | `3000` | no |  | How long the breaker stays open before probing Redis again. |
| `RATELIMIT_LEASE_FRACTION` | number (min 0, max 0.5) | `0.1` | no |  | Share of a hot policy's burst leased from Redis in one call and spent locally (0 disables the lease tier). The local tier never admits more than the global limit. |
| `RATELIMIT_LEASE_TTL_MS` | integer (> 0) | `1000` | no |  | Lifetime of a local lease. |
| `RATELIMIT_LOG_SAMPLE` | integer (> 0) | `100` | no |  | Log 1 in N limited decisions (policy id only, never raw keys). |
| `SHED_LOOP_LAG_MS` | integer (min 0) | `250` | no |  | Event-loop lag at which new connections and low-priority work are shed (0 disables). |
| `RATE_LIMIT_SCALE` | number (> 0) | `1` | no |  | Multiplies every rate limit. For load tests only; logged loudly at start-up when not 1. Never set this above 1 in production: it removes the protection. |

## Workers, jobs and sends

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKER_POOL_SIZE` | integer (min 0) | `2` | no |  | Worker threads for CPU-heavy tasks (large HTML sanitising). 0 = inline. |
| `WORKER_THRESHOLD_BYTES` | integer (min 0) | `32768` | no |  | Bodies larger than this go to a worker thread (measured threshold, docs/PERFORMANCE.md). |
| `SCHEDULER_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no |  | Run the background scheduler (jobs, snooze wake, digests, outbox relay) in this process. Turn off on web-only nodes. |
| `SEND_PACING` | boolean | `true` | no |  | Pace provider sends per number/sender (queue with a delay instead of rejecting). |
| `SEND_QUEUE_WORKSPACE_MAX` | integer (> 0) | `5000` | no |  | A workspace with more than this many sends waiting gets 429 on new external sends; other tenants are unaffected. |
| `SEND_RETRY_JITTER` | boolean | `true` | no |  | Randomise retry delays. |
| `SEND_QUEUE_MAX` | integer (> 0) | `500` | no |  | Global cap on queued sends per pass. |
| `SEND_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | integer (> 0) | `5` | no |  | Delivery attempts before a message is marked failed. |
| `SEND_RETRY_BASE_SECONDS` | number (> 0) | `30` | no |  | First retry delay; doubles each attempt. |
| `SEND_RETRY_CAP_SECONDS` | number (> 0) | `3600` | no |  | Largest retry delay. |
| `DIGEST_MIN_AGE_MINUTES` | number (> 0) | `2` | no |  | Unanswered contact messages younger than this are not yet in the email digest. |
| `DIGEST_MAX_AGE_MINUTES` | number (> 0) | `60` | no |  | Messages older than this are not in the digest. |

## SMS, email and webhooks

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SMS_PROVIDER` | `console` \| `twilio` | `console` | no |  | Platform default SMS provider, used by workspaces that have not connected their own Twilio account in Settings > Channels. `console` only logs: messages are stored as `not_sent_test_mode`; `twilio` sends them from this deployment's account. On a multi-tenant deployment leave it `console`: each workspace connects its own Twilio account. |
| `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` | string | unset | no |  | Twilio account SID (required with `SMS_PROVIDER=twilio`). **Secret.** |
| `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` | string | unset | no |  | Twilio auth token: sends SMS and verifies inbound webhook signatures. **Secret.** Rotate in the Twilio console and redeploy. |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `console` \| `sendgrid` | `console` | no |  | Platform default email provider, also used for system email (invitations, password reset, notifications). Workspaces connect their own SendGrid account in Settings > Channels for conversation email. `console` only logs. System email has no per-workspace provider: without `sendgrid` here, invitation and reset emails are only logged. |
| `SENDGRID_API_KEY` | string | unset | no |  | SendGrid API key (required with `EMAIL_PROVIDER=sendgrid`). **Secret.** |
| `SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY` | string | unset | no |  | Public key for verifying SendGrid event webhook signatures. **Secret.** |
| `WEBHOOK_SHARED_SECRET` | string | unset | no |  | Shared secret for SendGrid inbound parse (query `secret=` or `x-webhook-secret`) when signatures are unavailable. **Secret.** |
| `PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer (min 1000, max 120000) | `15000` | no |  | Time budget of every call to Twilio or SendGrid (sends, credential checks, imports); a slower answer counts as a timeout and is retried when it was a send. |
| `STUN_URLS` | string | `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302` | no | `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302` | Comma-separated STUN server URLs handed to both sides of a browser call. STUN alone connects peers on friendly networks only; behind symmetric NATs and many corporate or mobile networks a TURN relay is required (`TURN_URLS`, or the workspace's Twilio account). The default is a public Google server: set your own (coturn runs STUN too) if visitors' addresses must not reach a third party. |
| `TURN_URLS` | string | unset | no | `turn:turn.example.com:3478?transport=udp,turns:turn.example.com:5349?transport=tcp` | Comma-separated TURN URLs of your coturn server (`turn:turn.example.com:3478?transport=udp`, `turns:turn.example.com:5349?transport=tcp`). With `TURN_SECRET`, workspaces that choose the `static` TURN provider receive time-limited credentials per call. Render's free plan cannot host UDP TURN: run coturn elsewhere (docs/CALLS.md has a docker-compose and a Kubernetes sample). |
| `TURN_SECRET` | string | unset | no | `openssl rand -hex 32` | Shared secret of coturn's `static-auth-secret` (REST-style credentials: username `<expiry>:<call id>`, password HMAC-SHA1 of it). Never sent to browsers; only the derived, short-lived credentials are. **Secret.** Rotating it invalidates credentials already issued (calls in progress may drop when their relay allocation refreshes). Must match coturn's `static-auth-secret`. |
| `TURN_TTL_SECONDS` | integer (min 60, max 86400) | `3600` | no | `3600` | Lifetime of the TURN credentials issued for one call. A call that lasts longer restarts ICE with fresh credentials. |
| `WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS` | integer (> 0) | `300` | no |  | Replay window for signed webhooks (Stripe, SendGrid). |
| `SYSTEM_EMAIL_FROM` | string | `notifications@conversations.local` | no |  | From address of system email (invitations, reset, notifications, billing alerts). |
| `CREDIT_COST_SMS` | integer (min 0) | `1` | no |  | Credits one outbound SMS costs. |
| `CREDIT_COST_EMAIL` | integer (min 0) | `1` | no |  | Credits one outbound email costs. |

## AI

| Variable | Type | Default | Required | Example | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | string | unset | no |  | Enables the Claude-backed AI features. Without it, deterministic offline heuristics are used. **Secret.** |
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | string | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | no |  | Model id used for AI features. |
| `AI_TIMEOUT_MS` | integer (> 0) | `20000` | no |  | Timeout of one AI call; the feature degrades to heuristics on timeout. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | string | unset | no |  | Enables the optional `realtime` speech engine of AI calls: the server mints a short-lived client secret for ONE visitor call with this key; the key itself never reaches a browser or a log. Without it (or without `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL`) calls use the browser engine. **Secret.** Not exercised against the real service in this repository's tests (a local fake of the endpoints is). |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | string | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | no | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | Base URL of the OpenAI API used for client secrets and handed to the visitor's browser for the WebRTC call (`<base>/realtime/client_secrets`, `<base>/realtime/calls`). Change it for a proxy or a compatible service. |
| `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` | string | unset | no | `gpt-realtime` | Realtime model id for AI calls with the realtime engine. There is no built-in default: leave it unset and the realtime engine stays unavailable. |
| `OPENAI_REALTIME_VOICE` | string | unset | no |  | Voice id for the realtime engine. Unset: the provider's default voice. |
| `OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL` | string | unset | no |  | Model used to transcribe the visitor's speech in a realtime call (the transcript is what is stored in the thread and what the safety monitor reads). Unset: the provider's default. |
| `OPENAI_CLIENT_SECRET_TTL_SECONDS` | integer (min 10, max 7200) | `60` | no | `60` | How long the secret handed to the visitor's browser can open the realtime connection (it only has to last until the connection is made). |
| `AI_REALTIME_ENABLED` | boolean | `true` | no |  | Instance-wide kill switch of the realtime engine: false makes every workspace use the browser engine and ends running realtime calls. |
| `AI_REALTIME_COST_PER_MINUTE_USD` | number (min 0, max 100) | unset | no |  | Your own estimate of what one minute of a realtime call costs, used only to show an estimated cost in analytics. Unset: analytics shows minutes and no cost. |
